newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: President Aleman takes aim at tardy Nicaraguans.
newsitem.headline: President Aleman takes aim at tardy Nicaraguans.

text.p: Nicaragua's new President Arnoldo Aleman called on Friday for notoriously tardy Nicaraguans to show up to work on time to help jumpstart the country's tiny economy.
Aleman, who took office on Jan. 10, made a surprise visit on Friday to Nicaragua's Ministry of Health and found less than 100 of its 600 employees had showed up to work on time.
"I make a fraternal but firm call, since the government will fulfil its promise of job stability, for workers to be punctual and efficient in their work centres," Aleman said.
In his first two weeks in office, Aleman has made a number of surprise visits to government ministries to check on the habits of workers long used to showing up on what locals call "Nicaragua time."
In Nicaragua, news conferences often start hours late and public servants are accustomed to arriving late to work and taking long lunches.
But Nicaragua's new right-wing president has started a campaign to modernise sleepy Nicaragua, the second poorest country in Latin America after Haiti, and drag its economy into the modern world.
